snippets.text: ComfyUI and partners including Nvidia, Runpod, MiniMax, LTX and Black Forest Labs are offering $25,000 in prizes over two weeks for open-source builds on the Comfy Developer Platform, Comfy says.
snippets.why: The contest, which includes RTX 5090 cards for the most innovative, most viral and open-weights-only entries, is pitched as a response to Higgsfield's unfulfilled open-source promise.

snippets.text: OpenAI's developer account launched a site where people can browse hardware projects built with Codex by the community and submit their own, including a cat TV and a dream logger.
snippets.why: It shows what people are making with the coding agent beyond software, though OpenAI gave no count of projects or submissions.

snippets.text: Meta says its Omnilingual speech recognition suite, which covers over 1,600 languages including 500 with no prior ASR coverage, was named one of TIME's Best Inventions of 2026.
snippets.why: The coverage figures are Meta's own claims about the models, while the TIME listing is an editorial recognition rather than an independent test of accuracy.

snippets.text: Fal says OmniHuman V2 is live on its platform, generating talking videos from one image and an audio track with lip movements and expressions synchronised to speech, plus optional prompts.
snippets.why: Another route for developers to try audio-driven avatar video through an API, though fal published no pricing or quality comparison with the first version in the post.

snippets.text: Perplexity chief Aravind Srinivas said its API is now available inside Lovable apps, adding that adoption of the Perplexity API is expanding.
snippets.why: It gives people building apps in Lovable a built-in route to Perplexity's search-backed answers, though no usage figures were given.

snippets.text: Cursor says Meta's Muse Wonder is now in its editor, scoring 46.1% on CursorBench at default effort, the highest of any Muse model, at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output.
snippets.why: The benchmark is Cursor's own; the price matches what TechCrunch reported for Meta's API when Muse Wonder launched on October 12.

snippets.text: SemiAnalysis says Google submitted its first TPUv7 agentic benchmark result, claiming 1.42x better performance per dollar than Nvidia's GB300 NVL72 at FP4 and 2.5x better than AMD's MI355X.
snippets.why: The firm also says GB200 still holds a 1.2x edge at low interactivity, so the advantage depends on the workload and the cost basis it uses.

snippets.text: Theo says T3 Code, his coding-agent app, is out of alpha, in a post that had about 300 likes when read on Thursday.
snippets.why: It adds another independent coding front end to a field crowded with editor-based agents, though the post gives no feature list.

snippets.text: PrismML says it is running an open challenge with Darkbloom on Yukon Research to make its new Bonsai 2 9B model run faster, and that the model is also available through Darkbloom's API.
snippets.why: It is a community speed contest on a ternary 2 GB model, and the rules and prize are on Yukon Research rather than in the post.

snippets.text: Reuters reports, citing sources, that some Anthropic investors discussed a valuation near $1.5 trillion for an IPO, down from the roughly $2 trillion they had expected, after disclosures showed slower third-quarter revenue growth.
snippets.why: No IPO has been filed, and the figures come from unnamed sources, so the valuation talk could change before any listing.

snippets.text: The Information reports OpenAI is cutting ad rates in ChatGPT, chasing small and midsize advertisers and hiring talent from Meta as it grows its advertising business.
snippets.why: Lower prices aimed at smaller buyers suggest OpenAI wants ChatGPT ads to scale quickly, though the report is behind a paywall and OpenAI has not commented.

snippets.text: Google says more than 400 publications, including the Financial Times, CNN and the Texas Tribune, are now in its News AI pilot, which tests features such as article overviews, Nieman Lab reports.
snippets.why: The pilot is Google's test of AI summaries with publishers who have worried about lost traffic, so its expansion shows how many have agreed to take part.

snippets.text: Elon Musk posted a video captioned "Turns out the future does have flying cars", which drew more than 7,000 likes, alongside posts about a Tesla and SpaceX collaboration; no technical details were given.
snippets.why: It is a teaser, not a product launch, and the post does not say what the vehicle is, when it ships or whether AI is involved.
